3352431.title: 8th Daejeon Special Visual Effects Film Festival
3352431.overview: Korea's only film festival dedicated to VFX and special visual effects, built on Daejeon's visual-effects industry base. The program spans the DFX OTT Awards honoring effects work in Korean streaming content, DFX Screenings with director and cast talks, a DFX Tech Show on AI and VFX production trends, and DFX Pitch, which scouts feature-length effects-driven projects. Screenings spread across the DCC convention center and the city's independent cinemas. Free.
3352431.place: DCC Exhibition Hall 2 and cinemas across Daejeon

2699287.title: Eumseong Masterpiece Festival
2699287.overview: A farm-produce festival in Eumseong County, Chungbuk, showcasing and selling the region's agricultural goods and specialties. Expect produce exhibitions and direct sales, food booths, hands-on programs using local crops, and cultural performances — with growers and shoppers meeting face to face. A straightforward, local-flavored county fair rather than a tourist production.

2861680.title: 9th Jeonju International Short Film Festival
2861680.overview: A short-film festival in Jeonju's cinema street under the slogan 'New Frame, New Longtake' — this year expanding into vertical films shot for the phone screen while doubling down on short-form experimentation. The program combines screenings, audience talks with filmmakers, and a vertical-cinema forum at CGV Jeonju Gosa, in the heart of the city famous for its hanok village and food.

2616316.title: Suwon Jazz Festival
2616316.overview: An evening of jazz on the shores of Gwanggyo Lake Park — regularly ranked among Korea's best urban landscapes. Korean and international artists cover the spectrum from straight-ahead jazz to blues and funky crossover, aimed as much at casual listeners as aficionados. Free, outdoors, 17:30–21:30: bring a mat and settle in as the lake lights come on.

1390147.title: Anyang Dance Festival
1390147.overview: Anyang's citizen festival since 2000, drawing some 300,000 visitors a year and now one of Gyeonggi Province's flagship events. Under the slogan 'Walk, run, dance!', it treats any free movement of the body as dance, filling Pyeongchon Central Park and Samdeok Park with citizen performance teams, professional stages, and open dance floors over three days. Billed as Korea's only regional K-dance festival — and defiantly participatory: you will be invited to join.
1390147.place: Pyeongchon Central Park and Samdeok Park

3485135.title: Ocean Village
3485135.overview: A local market event on the Jangseungpo waterfront in Geoje, gathering the island's fresh farm and sea produce, small-batch foods from local makers, lifestyle goods, family items, street food, and hands-on programs in one strollable seaside venue. Runs Friday–Saturday 11:00–20:00 and Sunday to 18:00. A good graze-and-browse stop if you are touring Geoje's coast.

3524889.title: GES 2026: Game & Esports Seoul
3524889.overview: A global game and esports festival at Dongdaemun Design Plaza, hosted by the Seoul city government. Around 100 game and esports companies exhibit across indie and major-studio showcases, with esports tournaments (including a PUBG club match and the Seoul Cup), competitions, and networking programs drawing some 20,000 visitors. Free entry, 10:00–18:00 — three days of Korean gaming culture in one landmark venue.

3377089.title: Aragaya Culture Festival
3377089.overview: Haman's festival of Aragaya — the ancient Gaya confederacy kingdom whose royal tombs crown the UNESCO-listed Marisan mounds. Reenactments bring the kingdom to life: a royal procession, gate-guard changing ceremony, and mounted-warrior experiences, alongside history trails, youth-produced performances, and a fireworks-backed theme show, 'Ara Red Lotus'. Held at the Haman Museum and tomb park, 09:00–21:00, free — one of the best windows into Korea's less-told Gaya history.

3530743.title: Korean Confucian Culture Festival
3530743.overview: A festival translating Confucian values — loyalty, filial piety, propriety — into contemporary life, at the Korean Confucian Culture Promotion Institute in Nonsan, the heartland of Joseon's Confucian academies. Three days of performances, exhibitions, a humanities book concert, the K-Confucianism international forum, and family competitions and hands-on programs. Free entry (some programs paid). Pairs naturally with nearby Donam Seowon, a UNESCO World Heritage academy.
3530743.place: Korean Confucian Culture Promotion Institute and Noseong-myeon area

2555932.title: 11th Ulju Mountain Film Festival
2555932.overview: Asia's leading mountain-film festival, set at the welcome center of the Yeongnam Alps — the ridge country above Ulsan. The program spotlights how humans live with nature: trial and triumph, challenge and failure, conflict and coexistence, through international mountain films and documentaries that stretch the genre's boundaries. True to its setting, screenings include open-air bivouac and car-camping sessions running to midnight. Individual screenings 3,000 won; day pass 12,000 won.
2555932.fee: Screenings 3,000 won · Day ticket 12,000 won · UMFF pass 15,000 won · Bivouac screening 10,000 won

2999418.title: Peace Nuri Picnic Festival
2999418.overview: An autumn picnic-and-concert festival on the great lawns of Imjingak Pyeonghwa Nuri (Peace Park) near the DMZ in Paju. Spread a mat under open sky for the Peace special stage and live sets by popular Korean artists spanning generations — daytime picnicking rolling into evening concerts. Entry is a token 3,000 won. The venue itself, wind-turbine hills within sight of the border, is among Korea's most evocative concert settings.

1846818.title: Suseongmot Festival
1846818.overview: Daegu's lakeside arts festival at Suseongmot, the city's favorite evening hangout — twice ranked the city's best regional festival. The program floats between land and water: K-arts fantasy stages of Korean orchestral music, song, and dance, an on-the-water concert and 'wave' dance performance, street arts, a citywide youth dance competition, school music showcases, and an intangible-heritage stage. Music fireworks shows bookend the festival. Free, 13:00–22:00.

1078905.title: Yeonggwang Bulgapsan Red Spider Lily Festival
1078905.overview: Every September, millions of crimson spider lilies (sangsahwa) carpet the valley below Bulgapsa, a thousand-year-old temple on Bulgapsan Mountain. The 26th festival threads performances, exhibitions, and hands-on programs along the flower paths, with soft night lighting turning the fields into a second, quieter spectacle after dark. The flower — whose leaves and blossoms never meet — symbolizes impossible love, giving the walk its bittersweet undertone. Free, 10:00–21:00.

2997256.title: Pyeongchang Nongak & Mountain Food Festival
2997256.overview: A festival built around Pyeongchang Dunjeonpyeong nongak — the region's designated intangible-heritage farmers' music — in the highland township of Yongpyeong. The drumming and dance performances anchor a thoroughly edible program: pot-barbecue and skewer grilling, market-style gukbap stew, and other mountain-village food, plus folk games, madanggeuk theater, and hands-on traditions. Free entry (food paid), 10:00–20:00. As unpretentious and warm as festivals get.
2997256.place: Pyeongchang Nongak & Mountain Food festival grounds

3544886.title: Seoul Autumn Festa Opening
3544886.overview: The opening night of Seoul Autumn Festa — the city's 73-day performing-arts season running September 18 to November 29, when roughly 260 theater, dance, music, and traditional-arts productions play across the city. The kickoff concert at the Ttukseom Hangang Park riverside stage doubles as Seoul's declaration of itself as a performing-arts city. Free, 19:00–21:00, on the river as the season's first cool evenings arrive.
3544886.sponsor: Seoul Metropolitan Government · Seoul Foundation for Arts and Culture

624181.title: Namhansanseong Culture Festival
624181.overview: Three days marking the 400th anniversary of the fortress walls of Namhansanseong — the UNESCO-listed mountain fortress where a Joseon king withstood siege in 1636. Gwangju City's flagship festival mixes traditional and contemporary stage performances with history experience programs, participatory events, and a hands-on art market inside the provincial park. Free; the fortress wall walk itself, ringed with autumn forest, is reason enough to come.

2558735.title: Busan International Performing Arts Festival (BPAF)
2558735.overview: A street performing-arts festival along the Oncheoncheon stream and the university district near Pusan National University, staging everyday urban space as theater. The 2026 theme, 'MOSAIC: many pieces, one picture', brings 28 selected Korean and international productions to outdoor stages, joined by participatory side programs and an art market. Free, 13:00–20:00 — catch it while browsing one of Busan's liveliest student quarters.
2558735.place: Oncheoncheon stream and PNU university street

2029491.title: Gwacheon Performing Arts Festival (GPAF)
2029491.overview: Korea's first street-theater festival, running since 1997 and now drawing over 100,000 visitors each September. International and Korean companies stage outdoor and street productions across the plazas of Gwacheon, just south of Seoul, in a program mixing invited international works, Korean premieres, and commissioned pieces. Free and deliberately accessible — this is where Korean street theater made its name. 12:00–22:00.
2029491.place: Gwacheon Government Complex plaza and Citizens Hall area

2746930.title: Gamaksan Flower & Star Journey
2746930.overview: On the summit hill of Gamaksan in Geochang — the 'Star Wind Hill' — autumn wildflower fields bloom against one of southern Korea's best night skies. The sixth festival, themed 'a purple comma just for me', runs busking and sunset-hill concerts, a chrysanthemum-field walk, photo zones, a stamp tour, and a slow mailbox that delivers your letter before next year's festival. Local food tents serve bibimbap, gukbap, and jeon at village prices. Access by shuttle bus (3,000 won) or pre-booked private car.

2412052.title: Korea Youth Day Festival
2412052.overview: The 10th anniversary edition of Korea's official Youth Day festival, held on Gwangalli Beach in Busan. What began as an advocacy event became a legal commemoration day (third Saturday of September) in 2020, and the festival now spans youth policy, culture, careers, and entertainment: a K-pop concert, a college song contest, gala concert, youth film awards, the Korea cheerleading championship, and creator awards, all against the Gwangan Bridge backdrop. Free, 10:00–21:00.

140880.title: 67th Korean Folk Arts Festival
140880.overview: Korea's longest-running festival, held since 1958 to preserve and pass on regional folk performing arts — the event that historically surfaced many of the country's now-designated heritage traditions. The 67th edition gathers folk troupes from every province in Pyeongchang, the 2018 Winter Olympics host, for open-air performances at the Jinbu sports park. Free, 09:00–18:00: two days of farmers' music, mask dance, ritual, and song you will rarely see assembled in one place.
140880.sponsor: Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism · Gangwon · Pyeongchang

4106729.title: Mullae Arts Festival
4106729.overview: Mullae-dong is Seoul's strangest cultural ecosystem: precision metal workshops and artists' studios sharing the same alleys. Its festival opens that world up through three programs — 'Mullae Hyperlink' exhibitions linking the district's galleries, open studios where artists show work and process in place, and a street festival of performances, media facades, DJ sets, and markets in the alleys between lathes. Some programs need advance sign-up via the Yeongdeungpo foundation site. 12:00–19:00.

3493864.title: Gijang Pet Culture Festival
3493864.overview: A companion-animal festival in Busan's Gijang County themed 'happy coexistence with pets' — its third edition. New this year: a walk-together event for pets and owners, and 'K-Pet Got Talent', a national showcase for gifted dogs and cats. Experience, education, and participation programs run throughout, aimed at both pet owners and the pet-curious, with responsible pet culture and animal welfare as the through-line. Free, 09:00–18:00 at Jeonggwan Central Park.

2759788.title: Seoripul Music Festival
2759788.overview: For one weekend a year, Seoul closes the ten-lane Banpo-daero boulevard and turns it into a concert ground — the signature move of this Seocho district festival, which has drawn a cumulative 1.34 million visitors since 2015. The 2026 edition, 'Seocho is the Music', caps a month-long borough-wide music journey with two days of multi-genre stages and citizen programs on the open avenue. Free (market and food booths excepted).

3359644.title: Seokgye Station Moonlight Night Market
3359644.overview: A neighborhood night market at the culture park by Seokgye Station in northeast Seoul, run to boost the local alley economy. Food booths, craft beer and makgeolli, retro games, photo zones, and a flea market fill the park, with busking stages and headline performances (past editions have drawn well-known Korean singers). Booth prices vary; open 14:00–22:00. A low-key, genuinely local slice of Seoul night-market culture.

2851985.title: Uiwang Baekun Lake Festival
2851985.overview: Uiwang's autumn festival on the lawn plaza of Baekun Lake, a reservoir ringed by wooded hills just south of Seoul. Headline music performances share the bill with busking, free and paid hands-on programs, food courts, and events by local artists and residents — a community festival first, with the lake path there for strolling between acts. Free, 10:00–22:00.

2764526.title: Incheon Reading Festival
2764526.overview: Incheon's book festival at the Incheon Art Platform — a cluster of restored early-1900s port warehouses in the open-port district. Under the slogan 'Read Incheon, connect hearts', the outdoor plaza hosts picture-book performances, busking, a book market of local bookstores and publishers, photo zones, and a book-themed escape game, while indoor sessions run author meetings, book talks, and forums. Free, 11:00–17:00 — and the surrounding Incheon open-port streets and Chinatown make a full day of it.

1389228.title: Ansan Daebu Grape Festival
1389228.overview: Daebudo Island's sea-breeze vineyards produce unusually sweet, aromatic grapes, and this festival — running since 1995 — is their annual showcase. A direct-sale market cuts out the middleman for freshly picked bunches, while the signature grape-stomping event, concerts, the Daebu Haesol-gil walking festival, and the Ansan marathon fill the weekend at the Daebu Sea Fragrance Theme Park. Free, 09:00–18:00; an easy island day trip on Seoul's doorstep.

3538195.title: Gwangmyeong Book Festival
3538195.overview: Gwangmyeong's reading-culture festival on the lawn of the civic gymnasium, slogan: 'The start of infinite exploration, a friendly book journey!'. The grounds fill with hands-on programs, performances, author book concerts, and all-ages reading events designed to make books a shared outing rather than a solitary habit. Free, 10:00–17:00; program details on the city library website.

4107073.title: Mungyeong Eco-Camping Festival
4107073.overview: Camping, environment, and music meet on the banks of the Yeonggang River in Mungyeong. The program pairs the Yeonggang River Run with upcycling and recycling workshops that make resource circulation hands-on, plus family side events through the day. The closer is a headline hip-hop double bill — Dynamic Duo and Mighty Mouth — heating up the riverside autumn night. Free, 11:00–21:00.

2872196.title: Alien Festival
2872196.overview: Korea's only alien-themed festival, run by the Miryang Arirang Space Observatory — the country's observatory specializing in the search for extraterrestrial life. The 7th edition is styled as an 'alien sports day': Meteor Run races, laser tag, and a costume contest get families running rather than watching, with space-science content woven through for the educational payoff. Free, 10:00–18:00 at the Miryang stadium grounds.

3361182.title: Ulju Drone Festival
3361182.overview: A day of drones at Jakcheonjeong plaza in Ulju: balloon-popping and obstacle-racing drone games, drone basketball, plus AI baduk robots, an AI painter, quadruped robots, 3D printing, and a disaster-safety experience hall. Stages feature Chae Yeon, Lee Ji-hoon, Sleepy, and local crews. The finale is the point: a 1,300-drone light show choreographed to music over the autumn night sky — one of the larger drone shows on the Korean festival circuit. Free, 14:00–21:00.

4106842.title: Seoul Philharmonic Park Concert
4106842.overview: The Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra under music director Jaap van Zweden plays a free open-air evening at the Forest Stage of Seoul Children's Grand Park, joined by top-flight guest soloists. No reservation needed — just arrive and sit — and the concert streams live on the Seoul city and orchestra YouTube channels. 19:00–20:30. One of the easiest ways to hear a world-class orchestra for free.
4106842.place: Forest Stage, Seoul Children's Grand Park

3372236.title: Tuntun Pet Festa
3372236.overview: A two-day pet festival at Dongtan Yeoul Park in Hwaseong — a park already built for dogs, with its own pet playground. The fifth edition runs craft programs (walk bottle-bags, photo mugs), plus practical counseling corners: pet legal advice, health-check consultations, and behavior consultations, backed by the agriculture ministry and the Korea Kennel Association. Free entry, 10:00–18:00; bring the dog.

2829118.title: Haksan Madanggeuk Nollae Festival
2829118.overview: A citizen-created theater festival in Incheon's Michuhol district, running since 2014. Residents write and stage their own madanggeuk — open-air folk theater — drawing on neighborhood issues and life stories, in forms ranging from percussion drama and mask dance to puppet, music, and staged-reading theater. Performed outdoors by the artificial waterfall in Subong Park, it is community art in the most literal sense: the neighbors are the cast. Free, 17:00–21:00.

2845946.title: Youth Coffee Festival
2845946.overview: A coffee-and-culture festival on the plazas beneath Lotte World Tower, themed 'the perfect blend to wake today's me'. Korean and international coffee and dessert brands pour tastings, surrounded by photo zones and participatory programs, while the stage runs artist performances, youth talk concerts, auditions, classic screenings, and the 29-second film festival awards. Free, 13:00–18:00 — a caffeinated afternoon in Jamsil aimed at Seoul's twenty-somethings but open to all.
2845946.place: Lotte World Tower Arena Plaza and lawn

3062300.title: Gyeongju Golden Carnival
3062300.overview: A music festival with no main stage. Under the concept 'OFF THE STAGE', Gyeongju's old downtown — a shuttered cinema, empty storefronts, cafes, and alleys around the Hwangnidan and Geumnidan streets — becomes a constellation of small live venues, and the audience discovers performances rather than arriving at them. Local food and drink pace the wandering between sets. A one-ticket (55,000 won) experiment in using an ancient city's modern quarter as an instrument. 11:00–22:00.

141105.title: Gyeongnam Goseong Dinosaur World Expo
141105.overview: Goseong is one of the world's three great dinosaur-footprint fossil sites, and its expo — running since 2006, now in its 10th edition and 20th year — is Korea's flagship dinosaur event. The Danghangpo venue combines a dinosaur theme zone and an Admiral Yi Sun-sin zone with coastal walks, trails, and fossil-footprint paths. The 2026 theme is 'an exciting adventure with dinosaurs', with exhibitions, hands-on programs, and shows aimed squarely at families. Adults 19,000 won, children 13,000 won; open to 22:00 on night-opening days.

2818138.title: Changgyeonggung Palace Night Banquet
2818138.overview: A family-friendly night banquet at Changgyeonggung Palace, reinterpreting the feast Crown Prince Hyomyeong held for his father King Sunjo. Participants dress in court attire as Joseon officials and noblewomen, taste royal confections, watch traditional performances, and join palace experience programs around Munjeongjeon Hall. The autumn run spans late September through early October — including the Chuseok holiday — making it a natural family outing for the season. Sessions 17:00–20:30.
2818138.sponsor: Royal Palaces and Tombs Center, Korea Heritage Service

4080078.title: 2026 Korea Urban & Regional Innovation Expo
4080078.overview: Korea's largest urban-innovation expo, gathering government ministries, local governments, and companies around urban regeneration and regional innovation — exhibitions, seminars, and results-sharing sessions across four days at Osong Convention Center (OSCO) in Cheongju. Held annually since 2019 as a public-private-industry-academia forum. Free entry, 10:00–17:00 (to 15:00 Friday). A policy-and-industry event rather than a festival.
4080078.sponsor: MOLIT · Chungcheongbuk-do · Cheongju City · Yonhap News

229054.title: Ground Forces Festival
229054.overview: Korea's largest military culture festival, hosted by the ROK Army on the runway of Gyeryongdae — the tri-service headquarters. Five days of the latest Korean and US combat equipment on display (much of it climbable), Army TIGER and drone-bot demonstrations, AI-based combat systems at the army policy hall, and a full slate of military pageantry: military band and honor guard shows, taekwondo demonstrations, military police motorcycle drills, and road parades. Free, 09:00–17:00 over the Chuseok holiday window.

3006246.title: Busan International Performing Arts Market (BPAM)
3006246.overview: A festival-style performing-arts market in Busan, now in its fourth year: artists, producers, and presenters from Korea and abroad showcase productions, build networks, and negotiate distribution — but unlike a pure trade fair, the showcases are open for ordinary audiences to enjoy. Venues center on Dongseo University's Centum campus and the Haeundae Culture Center. Fees vary by program; 10:00–22:00.
3006246.place: Dongseo University Centum Campus and Haeundae Culture Center

3361334.title: Yeoncheon Goryeo Ginseng Festival
3361334.overview: Yeoncheon sits on the 38th parallel with the latitude, climate, and soil rated ideal for six-year ginseng — the gold standard of Korean insam. Its festival, in the plaza by Yeoncheon Station, showcases the county's Gaeseong-lineage Goryeo ginseng with exhibitions, direct farm sales, tastings, and hands-on programs, putting growers and buyers face to face. Free, 10:00–17:00. Good for stocking up at source prices on Korea's most famous health root.

613316.title: Cheongwon Life Festival
613316.overview: Cheongju's eco-agriculture festival, running since 2008 around the Cheongwon Life brand of premium local produce. The rural theme park in Ochang fills with themed exhibitions, hands-on farm programs, cultural performances, and a direct farmers' market connecting growers and consumers — with a strong education angle for children on where food comes from. Entry 5,000 won; children, teens, pregnant women, and seniors free. 10:00–20:00.
613316.fee: 5,000 won (children, youth, pregnant women, seniors free)

421977.title: Goseong Pollack Festival
421977.overview: Goseong on Gangwon's north coast was Korea's pollack capital, and this festival reworks that heritage on the beach at Geojin: a pollack gourmet zone with live chef cooking and cook-it-yourself sessions, fish crafts and games, bare-hand fish catching, a beach playground, and a silent-DJ party on the sand. Residents, soldiers, and students run much of the program themselves. Distributed stages and shuttles keep the beachfront lively all day. Free entry, 11:00–19:00.

2027215.title: Anheung Steamed Bun Festival
2027215.overview: Anheung's jjinppang — soft steamed buns with red-bean filling — made this Hoengseong village famous, and its 18th festival celebrates them with a full weekend: the bun-and-dokkaebi (goblin) themed main festival drawing on local folklore, the retro 'Saturday Saturday is a Singer' 90s-music stage, roaming goblin performance squads, bun-themed events, and a closing residents' singing contest. Free, 10:00–20:00, in the aptly named 'steaming bun village'. Come hungry.

1336591.title: Wanju Wild & Local Food Festival
1336591.overview: Wanju — the county that pioneered Korea's local-food movement — throws its flagship festival in the Gosan recreational forest under the 2026 slogan 'burning wild'. Fire is the theme: open-fire oven roasting, local bushcraft, potato pit-steaming, and large fire events, alongside stream water play, straw-bale slides, a 'local table' cooked by the women's associations of all 13 townships, a farm-produce market, and a wild EDM party after dark. Free, 10:00–22:00.

2856675.title: Anadream Safety Festival
2856675.overview: Gyeongbuk's largest safety-experience event, held since 2021 in the 'thousand-year forest' by the provincial office in Andong. Some 40 agencies run 70-plus hands-on safety programs — fire-engine and rescue-equipment displays, rescue-dog training demos, drone demonstrations, a firefighting parade, and a kids' safety school — leavened with magic and bubble shows, stamp tours, and treasure hunts. Free, 10:00–17:00, and genuinely useful for families with children.

2867143.title: Uiryeong Rich Rich Festival
2867143.overview: In the middle of the Nam River at Uiryeong stands Solbawi, the 'cauldron rock', with a legend: great fortunes will be born within 20 ri of it. The founders of Samsung, LG, and Hyosung were all born nearby — and the county has run with it. The fifth Rich Rich Festival invites visitors to soak up the rock's money-luck through wealth-themed experiences, performances, and family programs around town. Free (some programs paid), 10:00–22:00. Unapologetically fun feng-shui tourism.

1846797.title: Gunsan Time Travel Festival
1846797.overview: Gunsan preserves one of Korea's densest concentrations of Japanese colonial-era architecture, and its signature festival turns that district into a stage for time travel. Large flash-mob performances recreate the era's global currents, the 'March 5th' event fills the streets with the cry of the 1919 independence movement, and a time-currency system converts participation into souvenirs and discounts. Retro 7080 games and food round out a festival that manages to be both a history lesson and a proper day out. Free (some programs paid), 10:00–21:00.
1846797.place: Old city hall plaza and Time Travel Village

506766.title: Yeongju Punggi Ginseng Festival
506766.overview: Punggi is one of Korea's most storied ginseng regions, and its festival lands in October when the root's nutrients peak. The program leans into health: ginseng-cuisine tastings, ginseng-peeling contests, and wellness exhibitions, plus ritual reenactments — the founding-site rite, Governor Ju Se-bung's procession (the 16th-century official credited with starting cultivation here), and the great ginseng ceremony. Fresh roots, red ginseng, and processed goods sell at grower prices. Free entry, 10:00–20:00.
506766.place: Namwoncheon stream and Punggi Ginseng Park

1725929.title: King Jeongjo Filial Piety Festival
1725929.overview: Hwaseong's flagship history festival at Jeongjo Hyo Park, honoring the king whose devotion to his father shaped the region. The centerpiece reenacts the relocation of Crown Prince Sado's tomb to Yungneung — considered Joseon's finest burial site — and on October 4 the great royal procession of 1795 sets out from Dongtan Central Park in full period costume, one of Korea's grandest parade reenactments. Traditional performances and family programs fill the park throughout. Free, 10:00–18:00.

3380650.title: Dongdaemun Festival
3380650.overview: For one day, 700 meters of Janghan-ro go car-free under the theme 'a new gallop of culture' — a nod to the street's history, from the Joseon military horse pastures of Janghanpyeong to the modern used-car district. Performances, hands-on programs, and citizen events run the length of the road, including a pop-up roller rink and 'my car becomes a shop', where residents' own vehicles turn into market stalls. Free, 11:00–22:00.
3380650.place: Janghan-ro (700m, Woori Bank crossing to Jangan crossing)

1718424.title: Yeongju Museom Single-Log Bridge Festival
1718424.overview: Museom is a riverside heritage village wrapped in a bend of the Naeseongcheon stream, reached for centuries by a narrow single-log bridge over the water and white sand. The festival reenacts the village's life rites — a traditional wedding procession arriving by palanquin, a funeral bier procession departing — alongside bridge-crossing performances, barefoot sand walking, parade games, rope experiences, a poetry contest, a national photo contest, and a stamp tour. Free, 10:00–18:00. One of the most photogenic festivals in the country.
